title: introduce-ordinal-consensus-evaluator-and-failure-prioritizer
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds an ordinal-consensus-based evaluator that produces a stability matrix and a prioritized failure queue for CI-driven human review. Introduces a new CI hook that soft-fails on transient noise and hard-fails on sustained regressions. Backfilled historical baseline for 30 days.
description:
Motivation: Existing eval hooks focus on single-metric deltas (accuracy/bleu/qa scores) which miss cases where model outputs re-order relative preference across metrics and prompts. This PR introduces an Ordinal Consensus Evaluator that aggregates rank changes across multiple metrics to surface prompts with meaningful behavioral reordering instead of noise.

What this PR does: - Adds a new evaluator module `ordinal_consensus` which: computes per-prompt ordinal ranks across a configurable set of metrics, constructs a consensus matrix (pairwise rank agreement), and scores prompts by consensus drift. - Adds an auto-prioritizer that turns consensus scores into a ranked failure queue for SRE/QA to triage high-impact prompt regressions first. - Integrates the evaluator into the CI pipeline via a new lightweight hook `ci/hooks/consensus_gate.yml` which performs a three-stage decision: 1) quick noise filter (bootstrap across seeds) 2) conditional soft-fail if top-N instability is dominated by low-consensus metrics 3) hard-fail when the same prompts exceed the consensus drift threshold across two consecutive runs. - Backfills 30 days of historical data to compute context-aware thresholds and reduces false positives on nonstationary workloads. - Adds docs and a migration helper that maps existing single-metric alerts to the consensus view.

Checklist: - [x] Core evaluator implementation - [x] CI hook and gating logic - [x] Backfill pipeline (30-day job) - [x] Unit tests and integration smoke tests - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Performance sanity (runtime microbench added)

Why this is different: Instead of thresholding on raw metric delta values, ordinal consensus emphasizes changes in ordering (which often correspond to shifts in qualitative behavior). This captures regressions where one model variant begins to prefer a different answer style across prompts even when raw metric scores fluctuate within noise bands.

Operational notes: The consensus hook is conservative by default (soft-fail on first detection). Teams can opt into hard-fail via the project-level config: `.eval/config.yml -> consensus: { hard_fail_after: 2 }`. The backfill runs as a daily job and writes threshold snapshots to `eval-metadata/consensus-thresholds/`.

Migration and roll out: This was landed behind a feature flag `ORDINAL_CONSENSUS_ENABLED`. We enabled it for two internal repos for 48 hours and validated the top-20 queue against manual triage; observed 18/20 were meaningful regressions. After that we graduated to default-on for the main CI path with soft-fail semantics.

Risks and mitigations: - False positives during heavy prompt churn: mitigated by dual-run confirmation and seed-bootstrapped noise filter. - Performance: evaluator is O(M * P log P) for M metrics and P prompts; added an incremental windowed mode to bound run-time and cache pairwise agreements to avoid O(N^2) full recompute every CI run.

Related: ENG-7890 (stability initiative), ENG-8012 (CI gate consolidation), SUP-4123 (customer incident that motivated cross-metric reordering detection).
